think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 33-year-old pregnant woman at term (immigrant from Pakistan) presents with intractable back pain, bilateral suprasacral masses, L5 radiculopathy with left foot drop, and notable 1-year weight loss, found to have spinopelvic dissociation with extensive sacral osseous destruction, cold paraspinal abscesses tracking into the pelvis, and sparing of intervertebral discs. Standard diagnostic tests—AFB smear, mycobacterial bone cultures at 42 days, and molecular PCR amplification—were all negative, creating immense diagnostic challenge between culture-negative mycobacterial disease and sacral malignancy or pyogenic infection.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation concludes upon readmission at 40 weeks gestation with intractable back pain, left foot drop, neurological exam, triage CXR, CT pelvis, and MRI showing spinopelvic dissociation and multiseptated paraspinal abscesses with disc preservation, immediately prior to ultrasound-guided drainage, bone biopsy, PCR, and cultures.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus) typically causes rapid bony lysis and characteristically destroys adjacent intervertebral discs with high fever; here, the patient had an indolent 1-year course, afebrile presentation, disc space preservation ("good discs"), and multilocular cold abscesses. Primary or metastatic spinal/pelvic bone neoplasm (e.g., chordoma, giant cell tumor of sacrum, sarcoma) causes extensive sacral osteolysis and soft tissue masses, but the multilocular cystic fluid collections with peripheral thick capsule tracking into the psoas/paraspinal musculature and placental granulomas indicated an infectious granulomatous etiology.
case_prompt: A 33-year-old pregnant woman, originally from Pakistan and residing in the United Kingdom since 2014, presents to the emergency department at 40 weeks of gestation with intractable lower back pain, left L5 sciatica, and a newly developed left foot drop. She had been evaluated three weeks earlier at 37 weeks gestation for persistent back pain, L5 paresthesias, and S1-S2 numbness. Systemic history is notable for substantial weight loss over the preceding year without acute fever, cough, or bowel/bladder incontinence. Obstetric examination reveals a fetus small for gestational age, with symphysis fundal height measuring 33 weeks at 40 weeks gestation. Physical examination reveals bilateral suprasacral masses without overlying contusion, erythema, or signs of trauma. Neurological examination demonstrates MRC grade 4/5 left hip flexion (L2), 4/5 left knee extension (L3), 2/5 left ankle dorsiflexion (L4), 2/5 extensor hallucis longus dorsiflexion (L5), and absent left ankle reflex (S1-S2), with preserved perianal sensation and voluntary anal sphincter tone. Plain chest radiography demonstrates mild bronchial wall thickening and minimal linear scarring at the left lung base, without focal consolidation, cavitation, Ghon focus, or lymphadenopathy. Pelvic CT and spine MRI reveal spinopelvic dissociation with extensive osseous destruction of S1 and S2, bilateral paraspinal muscle edema, and a large thick-walled multiseptated collection (4.8 x 1.6 x 11.1 cm) tracking anteriorly through a defect in the right sacrum into the pelvic sidewall behind the iliopsoas muscle, with a second collection coursing through the left sacral wing into the greater sciatic notch. Intervertebral discs from L2 to S1 are preserved without disc space destruction.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis / bacterial osteomyelitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic spinal infection typically presents with acute febrile toxicity, rapid bony erosion, and prominent destruction of the intervertebral disc spaces; in contrast, imaging demonstrated preserved disc spaces ('good discs') despite extensive sacral osteolysis, indolent progression, and sterile extended bacterial cultures.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Vertebral discs were spared (good discs); however, there were disc bulges from the L2-3 to L5-S1 levels... Microbiology sample revealed that acid-fast bacilli were not detected, and TB culture bottles revealed no growth after 42 days.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary pelvic bone neoplasm or metastatic sacral malignancy
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Extensive sacral osteolysis and bilateral suprasacral masses accompanied by chronic weight loss raised suspicion for a primary sacral malignancy (such as chordoma or giant cell tumor) or metastasis, but cross-sectional MRI confirmed multiseptated, thick-walled fluid-filled cold abscesses tracking across fascial planes.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The collection appears hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2, and STIR with multiple internal septae and a thick wall suggestive of an abscess

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although bone aspirate AFB microscopy, molecular PCR, and 42-day mycobacterial cultures were negative, histological examination of the placenta delivered post-partum identified characteristic chronic granulomata within chorionic villi, confirming extrapulmonary tuberculosis as the cause of spinopelvic destruction.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A sample from the placenta detected two small granulomata within the chorionic villi. These samples were taken after delivery but notably after the TB treatment was initiated.

editor_comments: Extrapulmonary spinal tuberculosis (Pott disease) can involve the sacrum and pelvis, causing spinopelvic dissociation and cold abscesses that spare the intervertebral disc spaces—a hallmark distinguishing it from pyogenic spondylodiscitis. Culture-negative and PCR-negative extrapulmonary disease occurs in up to 50% of paucibacillary cases, where placental or peripheral tissue histopathology can provide essential diagnostic confirmation.
